species.name: Anablemum lithicum

diagnostic_hints.description: Embolus basally broad and flat, arising retrolaterally and coiling anticlockwise in a tight spiral; outer process robust and projecting prolaterally, inner process shorter and nearly straight; apices closely aligned but unfused.
Long sinuous ducts extend to large copulatory openings near the anteromedial margins of each fossa, rather than the mediolateral openings of A. pilosum.

habitat_ecology: Associated with rocky habitat; this is stated in the etymology, not presented as a diagnostic character.

species_level_identification.limitations: The diagnosis relies on male palpal or female epigynal structure. Locality and rocky habitat are supporting context only.

diagnostic_hints.description: Trilobate transverse band of grey-white scales across the anterior ocular quadrangle, with shallow paired depressions flanking the fovea and no longitudinal stripes on the dorsal opisthosoma.
Rounded bulbous tegulum with a narrow, acutely angled tegular lobe projecting prolaterally.

species_level_identification.limitations: Known in the thesis only from males. External pattern can support a suggestion, but palpal structure provides the stronger separation from congeners.

diagnostic_hints.description: Dense clypeal fringe of thick white setae and legs III the longest pair; the otherwise similar H. scutulatum lacks the fringe and has legs I longest.
Narrow tubular embolic disc with a short, thick, strongly curved embolus.
Proportionally large posterior spermathecae and thick elbowed copulatory ducts, contrasting with the smaller spermathecae and straighter ducts of H. scutulatum and H. griseum.

species_level_identification.limitations: The male fringe and leg proportions support a suggestion; confirmation is strongest from the palp or epigyne.

diagnostic_hints.description: Distinctive blue-silver clypeal fringe.
Terminally truncate taller inner embolic apex tapering distally, with a shorter, narrower and pointed outer apex.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. The clypeal fringe is photographically useful, but the source diagnosis combines it with palpal structure.

diagnostic_hints.description: Prominent brushes of iridescent blue-green setae extend laterally from the medial parts of the palpal tibiae, cymbia and patellae; unlike J. auripes, the male lacks an orange fringe on femora I and II.
Compact embolic disc with two thick apices; the inner apex has a medial tooth-like projection and truncate tip, and the outer is slightly shorter, narrower and pointed.
Darker overall than J. braccatus and lacks that species' triangular arrangement of three dark-setal patches near the posterior dorsal opisthosoma; genitalic proportions also differ subtly.

species_level_identification.limitations: The male palpal brushes are conspicuous. Female separation includes subtler somatic and genitalic comparisons and should remain tentative without expert examination.

species.name: Jotus citreus

diagnostic_hints.description: Clypeus densely covered with orange setae and chelicerae bright yellow.
Compact embolic disc with two narrow apices and a tooth-like projection near the base of the inner apex; in J. aurora the comparable tooth lies about halfway along the apex.

habitat_ecology: Collected at the edge of a management trail beside a small rainforest-creek crossing in unburnt riparian cool-temperate rainforest.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. Facial colour is useful for suggestion, while the source diagnosis also relies on the position of the embolic tooth.

species.name: Jotus rubripes

diagnostic_hints.description: Ventral and ventrolateral surfaces of femora and patellae I densely covered with bright red-orange setae; dorsal palpal segments are dark and clothed in long dark setae.
Compact embolic disc; inner apex truncate with a rounded bump around mid-length, outer apex much shorter, narrower and finely pointed.

habitat_ecology: Collected in mixed open dry and wet sclerophyll forest with grassy understorey and scattered granite boulders; the site had burned within the preceding 12 months.

species_level_identification.limitations: Known in the thesis only from the male. The leg-I colour is source-diagnostic, but habitat and locality are supporting context only.

diagnostic_hints.description: Dorsum densely clothed in silvery-blue iridescent scales with a small central circular-to-oval dark patch slightly behind mid-length.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. Iridescence depends on illumination and viewing angle, so photographs should show the entire dorsal abdomen under useful light.

diagnostic_hints.description: Two discrete subovate patches of black scales, rather than the two longitudinal black tracts of M. chrysomelas; the pattern resembles a clothing button.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. The suggestion depends on a clear dorsal view and verified Micromaratus genus placement.

diagnostic_hints.description: Vivid red scales form a dense mat across the clypeus about as broad as the anterior median eyes.
Broad full-length longitudinal tract of white scales bordered by dense black scales, with additional narrow white dorsolateral tracts.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown and the type record lacks precise coordinates. Facial and dorsal patterns should both be confirmed; locality alone is not identifying evidence.

species.name: Micromaratus sandersae

diagnostic_hints.description: Three longitudinal pairs of iridescent scale patches positioned on either side of the dorsal midline.
Females resemble other Micromaratus and may not be identifiable without association with a male or molecular data.

habitat_ecology: Type series collected by sweep net from a grassland shrub.

species_level_identification.limitations: The dorsal pattern supports males. Do not offer a confident female suggestion without an associated male or molecular evidence.

diagnostic_hints.description: Unbroken medial longitudinal band of white scales extends the full dorsal length and tapers posteriorly; pedipalps are bicoloured with pale, white-setose femora and patellae but dark tibiae and cymbia.
Embolus compact and slender; inner apex taller and thicker than the outer and terminally truncate, unlike the broader, longer configuration of externally similar S. deceptus.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. Externally resembles S. deceptus; the abdominal stripe alone must not be treated as diagnostic.

species.name: Striattus aridus

diagnostic_hints.description: Embolic disc extremely long, coiled anticlockwise in a wide spiral nearly encircling the tegulum, with the embolus bifurcate distally.
Long copulatory ducts loop behind and partly encircle the moderately sized posterior spermathecae.
In life, flattened recumbent white setae form dense patches on palpal femora and patellae, contrasting with dark cymbia and tibiae.

distribution.locality: 10 km northeast of Toulby Gate, Culgoa Floodplain National Park

habitat_ecology: The thesis characterises the occurrence as arid habitat; the type series was collected in a pitfall trap.

species_level_identification.limitations: The unique source diagnosis is primarily genitalic. Palpal setae and arid occurrence are supporting evidence only.

diagnostic_hints.description: Embolic disc basally broad and robust; outer apex much taller and thicker than the narrow inner apex and reaches near the distal cymbial margin.
Copulatory openings at the exterior posterolateral fossa margins lead through short, thick, elbowed ducts to large rounded spermathecae.

species_level_identification.limitations: Externally very similar to S. annulatus. A confident suggestion requires examination of the male palp or female epigyne.

diagnostic_hints.description: Glossy black dorsum with a medial white scale tract interrupted in the posterior third, forming an exclamation-mark-like figure.
Posterior spermathecae ovate, longer than wide and close together; short ducts curve strongly posterolaterally, with openings near the posteromedial fossa margins.

species_level_identification.limitations: The male dorsal mark is photographically useful. Females are externally similar to congeners and require epigynal examination.

diagnostic_hints.description: Generally paler than congeners, with longitudinal striping on the ocular quadrangle contrasting with a grey-scaled background.
Compact embolic disc with two short, thick apices that appear fused distally.
Openings at the outer anterolateral fossa margins; long narrow ducts curve posterolaterally and cross to the mediolateral margins of large rounded spermathecae.

species_level_identification.limitations: Pale colour and ocular striping support a candidate, but confirmation should use the palp or epigyne.

species.name: Tropijotus cavernus

diagnostic_hints.description: Posterior dorsum covered with iridescent violet-turquoise scales; anterior dorsum has a distinctive white patch on a dark blue to nearly black background.
Embolic disc terminates in three apices: the innermost shortest, narrowest and sharply pointed; the outer two reach equal height and taper distally.

habitat_ecology: Holotype collected from the outer surface of a cave wall; the thesis characterises the habitat as the outer surfaces of the Chillagoe caves.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. Iridescent colours vary with viewing angle; cave association and locality are supporting evidence only.

diagnostic_hints.description: Anterior eye row and ventral femoral surfaces of legs I bear vivid red scales; body and legs carry sparse scales iridescing purple to green.
Inner embolic apex much narrower and shorter and slightly prolaterally projecting; outer apex thicker, taller and bifurcate distally.
Broad transverse band of off-white setae at the anterior dorsal opisthosomal margin; T. ornatus females lack discernible dorsal patterning.

species_level_identification.limitations: Female genitalia closely resemble T. ornatus and may be difficult to identify without an associated male or molecular data. Female dorsal pattern is supportive, not independently definitive.

species.name: Tropijotus galacticus

diagnostic_hints.description: Bright orange setae on the ventral femora of legs I and II and a dorsum densely covered in purple-to-green iridescent scales; lacks the long white abdominal fringe of T. nebulosus.
Small anterior spermathecae positioned around the mediolateral fossa margins, rather than reaching or passing the anterior margins or being absent.

habitat_ecology: Type series collected at 1100 m elevation in an intercept trap.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male iridescence depends on viewing angle. Female suggestions require epigynal examination.

diagnostic_hints.description: Bright red clypeal fringe combined with bright yellow chelicerae.
Two fused embolic apices: inner slightly shorter, truncate and about equal in width; outer taller and truncate.
Large, slightly angular posterior spermathecae with much smaller subovate anterior spermathecae.

species_level_identification.limitations: The male facial combination is conspicuous. Females require epigynal examination; locality is not diagnostic.

diagnostic_hints.description: Prominent brushes of long, highly iridescent setae extend laterally from the medial cymbia and palpal tibiae.
Two fused embolic apices: inner shorter and much narrower; outer taller and truncate.
Small pear-shaped anterior spermathecae.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male palpal brushes are photographically useful but iridescence varies with angle. Female suggestions require examination of the epigyne.

diagnostic_hints.description: Prominent fringe of long white setae surrounds the opisthosoma, whose dorsum is covered with iridescent green scales.
Inner embolic apex shorter but about as wide as the outer and bifurcate distally; outer apex taller and truncate.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. The white fringe and iridescent dorsum should be observed together; colour varies with illumination.

diagnostic_hints.description: Ventral femoral surfaces of legs I are distinctively black and shiny.
Inner embolic apex shorter, narrower, twisted and notched distally; outer apex taller, broader and trifurcate.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. A ventral or lateral view of femora I is needed; dorsal-only photographs may miss the source-diagnostic character.

diagnostic_hints.description: Anterior median eyes bordered ventrally by light-brown to yellow scales; pale proximal palpal segments bear long light-yellow setae, while the cymbium is dark with grey-to-black setae.
Large ovate posterior spermathecae and smaller kidney-shaped anterior spermathecae extending beyond the anterior fossa margins.
Dorsal opisthosomal markings resemble those of the male.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male colour combination is useful but requires clear facial and palpal views. Female confirmation should use the epigyne.

diagnostic_hints.description: Long vivid-orange setae on the ventral femoral surface extend laterally, with a prominent blue-grey fringe on the lateral tibiae and metatarsi I.
Inner and outer embolic apices are separated proximally, unlike the proximally fused apices of T. fortiniae.
Lacks discernible dorsal opisthosomal patterning; T. fuchsia females have an anterior transverse off-white band.

species_level_identification.limitations: Female genitalia strongly resemble T. fuchsia and may not be identifiable without an associated male or molecular evidence. The female absence of a pattern is only supportive.

diagnostic_hints.description: Bicoloured fringe: a thick white transverse fringe below the anterior eye row and a vivid orange fringe above the chelicerae.
Two fused ribbon-shaped embolic apices; inner shorter, narrower and sharply pointed, outer taller, broader and truncate.
Ducts form elbowed distal sections and anterolateral lobes before reaching anterior spermathecae held tightly against the medial ducts.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male facial pattern is conspicuous. Female suggestions require epigynal examination. The spelling 'wondul' follows the species treatment; the genus composition list elsewhere has 'wondu'.

diagnostic_hints.description: Male with alternating black-and-white transverse zigzag markings; female with pale chevron-like dorsal markings.
Distinctive distal projection on the inner embolic apex.
Anterior spermathecae absent or strongly reduced, without distinct sclerotised chambers.

species_level_identification.limitations: Dorsal pattern is useful in both sexes, but female confirmation is stronger when the reduced anterior spermathecae can be examined.

diagnostic_hints.description: No long-setal fringes on legs III; two oblique white dorsal tracts are each interrupted three times, producing paired symmetrical zigzag or stepped patches.
Embolus longer than in congeners, reaching at least halfway up the cymbium in ventral view.
Larger fossae and more rounded duct diverticula than U. spectabilis, which has smaller fossae and elongate proximal receivers with an elbowed duct curve.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male dorsal pattern and absence of leg-III fringes are photographically useful. Females require epigynal comparison.

diagnostic_hints.description: Dense orange clypeal setae and long iridescent leg-III setae appearing blue to purple; compared with U. bimaculatus, whose clypeus is blue and yellow and leg-III fringe black.
Lacks the two transverse white tracts on the posterior third of the dorsal opisthosoma that occur in U. bimaculatus.
Posterior spermathecae ovate and wider than long; those of U. bimaculatus are more elongate with a medial constriction.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male colour characters are conspicuous but iridescence varies with angle. Female absence of white tracts is supportive; epigynal confirmation is preferable.

diagnostic_hints.description: Prominent bright-white tuft extends anteromedially above the anterior median eyes, combined with dense orange scales or setae on the clypeus and between the anterior eyes.
Small rounded-to-elongate diverticula are diagonally oriented anteromedially, rather than transversely as in other congeners or large and anterior as in V. zabkai.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male facial ornamentation is photographically useful. Females require epigynal examination.

diagnostic_hints.description: Elongate legs III with white setal fringes on the metatarsi; the similar V. mutans has dark-brown to black fringes.
Compact embolic disc lacks the thick proximal flange present on the more rounded disc of V. mutans.

species_level_identification.limitations: Females are unknown. White leg-III fringes support a candidate, but palpal comparison is recommended against V. mutans.

diagnostic_hints.description: Dense mat of orange scales covers the ocular quadrangle; dorsal pedipalps are distinctly bicoloured with a prominent long white fringe just before the cymbium.
Small triangular process adjacent to the base of the inner embolic apex.
Large round fossae with posteromedial openings; long ducts follow short winding, tangled paths; round diverticula lie near the anterior fossa margins.

species_level_identification.limitations: Male orange ocular scaling and bicoloured palps are useful in photographs. Female suggestions require epigynal examination.
